statusText: Mapped policy state: BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES (orange). NQ front month is quoted at 28,880.25, down 1.72%, only about 64 points above the 28,816.25 session low after the earlier bounce to roughly 42% of the session range faded back to about 22%. VIX has recovered to 17.86 from 17.59 an hour ago, the 2Y has turned from easing to 4.66% and up 2.8 basis points, the 10Y sits at its 4.989% session high, and WTI has extended to $103.76, up 3.71%. Tail rises five points to 26 into the 13:30 UTC cash open.
recommendation: Tail at 26 sits in the elevated band, so the mapped state is BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The danger window is held at 13:00-16:00 UTC, covering the 13:30 UTC cash open and the first two cash hours, because that transition is the session's first genuine liquidity transfer of a gap of about 1.7%. Conditional Tail peaks at 28 in the 14:00 UTC hour, seven points below the strong-block threshold, and returns to the watch band from 16:00 UTC as gap absorption normally completes. From 21:00 UTC the conditional path reaches the EA_ON mapping across the thinnest overnight hours, then drifts back toward the watch band ahead of Tuesday's US data block. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: The premarket bounce fades back to within 64 points of the 28,816.25 low while VIX, the 2-year yield and crude all turn higher together; Tail rises to 26 with the danger window held at the 13:00-16:00 UTC cash open
body:
The de-escalation recorded in the 11:00 and 12:00 UTC assessments has partly reversed in the final premarket hour. As of 13:15 UTC, NQ front month is quoted at 28,880.25, down 506.75 points or 1.72% against a 29,387.00 reference. The 28,816.25 session low set around 10:15 UTC is still intact and the sequence of consecutive lower lows remains broken, but the contract now sits only about 64 points above that low, roughly 22% of the 28,816.25 to 29,111.00 range, against about 42% an hour ago. That is a retracement that has failed to hold rather than a consolidation, and a failing retracement into a scheduled liquidity transfer is one of the named amplifiers of a path that denies mean reversion. The December contract quoted on a separate venue shows the same broad shape, trading in the lower half of its own session range, so the structure is not an artifact of one feed.

Cross-asset evidence has also re-aligned. VIX at 17.86 is up 12.74% on the day and has recovered from the 17.59 print measured an hour ago toward its 18.17 session high, so implied volatility is rebuilding rather than decaying. The 2-year yield has turned from easing to 4.66%, up 2.8 basis points, and the 10-year at 4.989% is trading at the top of its 4.973 to 4.989 session range. Both legs of the curve are now extending against equities rather than cushioning them. WTI has extended to $103.76, up 3.71%, with Brent at $108.82, up 4.02%, above the levels quoted in the morning wires. Four independent amplifiers moving the same way at the same time is a materially different picture from the split tape of the previous two hours, and Tail rises five points to 26.

The catalyst stack behind the move is unusually dense and is verified. Reuters reports that an essay from Anthropic's chief executive calling for a slower pace of AI capability advancement, publicly supported by the heads of xAI and OpenAI, triggered a reassessment of AI-linked valuations, with Intel down 6.5%, AMD down 5.5% and Marvell down 7.5% in premarket trade. Al Jazeera reports that Saudi Arabia closed its East-West pipeline, the primary export route around the blockaded Strait of Hormuz, after drone strikes launched from Iraqi territory, and Reuters reports that a scheduled Iran-Gulf meeting in Oman on reopening the strait was postponed. A hotter-than-expected US consumer price report on Friday has moved markets to price roughly an 86% to 89% probability of a 25 basis point Federal Reserve increase on Wednesday, which would be the first since 2023, alongside about 76% odds of a Bank of Japan increase on Friday.

Several de-amplifiers keep this well short of the strong-block band. ES is down only 0.67% against the Nasdaq's 1.72%, which points to a sector-specific repricing rather than a broad risk-off flush. Reuters reports ServiceNow up 4.7% and Adobe and Workday each up 2.3% as investors position for reduced AI disruption risk, so the index is rotating internally rather than liquidating uniformly, and dispersion of that kind normally raises Stress and lowers directional conviction rather than raising Tail. The session low has now survived more than three hours, and a VIX at 17.86 is a modest absolute level for a tape carrying this many catalysts. Stress rises to 79 at the top of the high band, while Tail stays eight points below the strong-block threshold.

The danger window is held at 13:00 to 16:00 UTC, covering the 13:30 UTC cash open and the first two cash hours, because the opening auction is the session's first genuine price discovery for the gap. Conditional Tail peaks at 28 in the 14:00 UTC hour and steps back to the watch band from 16:00 UTC, on the assumption that gap absorption completes in the first two cash hours. Nothing about the opening structure is observable yet, so that elevation reflects a scheduled transition and the current amplifier count, not an observed post-open path. Confidence is 87: the price, volatility, rates, energy and calendar evidence is current and verified from primary sources, and the shared cross-asset context file was stale at collection time and carried an unavailable calendar section, so it was not used as evidence for this assessment.

lookbackSummary: Over the past 24 hours the Claude series ran through the low band during Sunday's US evening, entered the watch band from 21:00 UTC as the oil and AI stories developed, and moved to the elevated band at 09:00 and 10:00 UTC when NQ set a sequence of lower lows into 28,816.25 with a trend-down mode. It stepped back to the watch band at 11:00 and 12:00 UTC as that low held and the bounce steadied near 42% of the session range. Stress stayed in the high band throughout, between 68 and 79, and Confidence improved to 88 as live price evidence became available. All 24 hourly slots are available from published Claude history.
outlookSummary: The 24-hour outlook is built around the 13:30 UTC cash open. Conditional Tail holds in the elevated band for the current hour and the first two cash hours, peaking at 28 at 14:00 UTC, then returns to the watch band from 16:00 UTC on the assumption that a gap of about 1.7% is absorbed in the first two cash hours. The conditional path then decays through the US afternoon, with a one-point nudge for the 19:00 UTC power hour, and reaches the low band across the thin overnight and Asian hours before drifting back toward the watch band during the European morning and into Tuesday's ADP and Empire State releases at 12:15 and 12:30 UTC. Confidence declines steadily with distance from the last verified price observation. Every hour beyond the current one is conditional risk, not observed structure.
